notes: Large-source-unit candidate 5 (s005 s006 s007 → 'pleaseth') is genuinely indivisible: the morphemes are contiguous, one English word carries the adjective, the preposition and its construct noun together, and no word is spent on any one of them, which is rule 40's reading of רַע בְּעֵינֶיךָ → 'displease'. The suffix keeps the 'him' written for it under rule 18.

Large-source-unit candidate 28 (s029 s030 s031 → 'him that pleaseth') holds on the same terms: 'pleaseth' fuses the three morphemes and the supplied 'him that' is what rule 46 hands to the whole anarthrous substantive, which rule 30 says does not defeat its one-rendering condition. Splitting would leave לִ or פְּנֵי unrepresented beside a morpheme holding the whole word, which rule 30 forbids in both directions.
The italic 'God' at t008 is a supplied lexical subject answering to no morpheme and is added under rule 17.
